hypotheses.reasoning: The 502s on POST /v1/notify come from api-gateway reporting 'upstream notification-svc connection reset (no healthy upstream)' (e.g. #3725, #3771, #4093), but those are downstream symptoms. The origin is notification-svc memory: at 14:23:36 (#2704) it reports heap at 78% after full GC with old gen not reclaimed, meaning messageCache is growing without eviction while young GC looks normal. The heap then exhausts (#3631 at 14:28:00 'heap exhausted while growing messageCache'), the OOM-killer restarts the pod (#3634), and the JVM OOMs again (#3984, #4376) with repeated OOMKilled restarts (#3985, #4377). Each restart drops the instance, so the gateway gets connection resets and 502s in bursts. Ruled out: the status_v2 schema error in accounts-db/account-svc (#3427, #3591) only affects /login through account-svc and is unrelated to notify; the report-cron pandas failure and the legacy-inventory healthcheck timeouts in status-poller are unrelated background noise.

Alternative reading: the gateway 502s and restarts could be amplified by client retries against the restarting notification-svc. The gateway lines only show the impact, and the trigger is the memory growth, so this is a secondary effect rather than the origin.

verdict.recommendedAction: Treat notification-svc memory as the fix priority. Capture the heap dump at /tmp/heap.hprof to identify what is retaining objects in messageCache, and add a bound or TTL/eviction to messageCache. As a short-term mitigation, raise the memory limit or restart on a schedule and scale out notification-svc replicas so that one OOM does not drop all healthy upstreams. Separately, track the accounts.status_v2 missing-column migration (account-svc /login 500s) and the report-cron pandas dependency as their own issues.
